issue_context.title: Use watch connection to get old leases in leader election
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Maintain a watch connection to synchronize the lease with kube-apiserver instead of [getting](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/resourcelock/leaselock.go#L42) the lease via a GET request 

### Why is this needed?

Every time a leader election client tries to update lease, it needs to get the old lease first to check identify and time, which has a few issues:

* APF concurrent share for leader election by default is quite low (i.e. 10), it could be too small in small machines hosting kube-apiserver. Using watch connection would reduce 50% leader election requests.
* Getting lease without specifying `resourceVersion` takes slight more resource from `kube-apiserver` to serve. When under load, `kube-apiserver` might be failed to response within timeout.

One major risk of doing is the client may get stale leases and decide to take the lease. I haven't looked into the code of handing lease PUT requests, but I think it should be taken care of to avoid giving up lease prematurely since there is not guarantee about freshness of GET response anyway.
comments:
Hello, @linxiulei  
I like your idea of using a watch connection to sync the lease with kube-apiserver. 
This could improve the cluster performance and reliability by reducing the number of requests to kube-apiserver, saving the resource consumption of kube-apiserver, and avoiding the risk of getting stale leases.

@linxiulei 

However,  I also see some difficulties and costs in doing this.

like,  what if the watch connection breaks or drops? 
This could cause the leader election to fail or be delayed. A possible solution is to use a retry mechanism or a backup connection to restore the sync. And to ensure that the watch connection does not add more load or complexity (so that this doesn't affect the performance and reliability of the cluster), we could use a lightweight protocol or a compression technique to reduce the data transfer and processing.

Catching up on it - let me share some thoughts on it:

1) I'm -1 on using watch for a leader. We need to do our best to ensure that we will not loose the leader lock after we already acquired it and it will be more likely if leases face higher watch latency [which we observed in the past].

2) That said for the leader we know that only the leader should be updating the lease. So we can do the simplest possible thing by:
- optimistically assuming that the result of our previous write is the current version
- in case of conflict, falling back to "GET + PUT again"
I'm +1 on the above

3) I guess I could probably live with watch *provided* we will only do that for non-leader.
In this case, lagging watch effectily only impacts the inability of a given component to take over the leader lock or some additional calls when the lock was already acquired by a different instance in the meantime.
That said, before I agree with that, I would like to see some fallback mechanism to "GET+PUT" and I would like to understand how it would work.

Note that the additional advantage that I see for non-leader is that with default RetryPeriod=2s and default LeaseDuration=10s, on average only 1 per 2.5 calls are useful [the other are useless because nothing changed in the meantime], so we would effectively also save a bit of resources on processing those.

@liggitt - FYI

@wojtek-t Your ideas roughly matched what I had in mind with extra safe measures. Thanks!

I made a [PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122049) with some polishes needed to be done. PTAL!

review_comments:
You can enter this path also if you didn't enter the original one [e.g. because lease wasn't valid].
So the removed lines should stay here.

This has in theory unbounded cardinality - we shouldn't make a name to be a label.

Why do we need a name? If we really need to check the name, we should use logs - for metrics we should focus oncount.

OTOH - I see other metrics above to be labeled with name - isn't that an issue?

@dgrisonnet @logicalhan ^^
What name is this? If it's a per-cluster (or per control-plane node) name it should be practically bounded and we've traditionally been okay with this.

It's "per component taking part in leader election".

So in general yes - it should be bounded [modulo bugs etc.]. So I'm assuming this is fine for you...

Also nit:
```
switch updates {
case 2; return ..
case 4: return ...
}
```

I'm not entirely sure how this metric will be used - the fact that it's say 1000 is not meaningful if we don't know how many "fast path" there were. If for fast_path we had 100, that's bad, if for fast_path we had 1000000, that's great.

Shouldn't we rather have a metric that is labeled with "method" with values "fast_path" and "slow_path" or sth like that?

Correct me if I'm wrong. The counter is cumulative so we can query to see the rate/delta of this counter and the users should know the rough frequency of leader election requests (i.e. once every 2s) then they know the rough percentage of slow_path being exercised.

I avoided reporting "fast_path" for performance consideration (current metric reports only when leader is switched, which is low overhead) because it's likely the case and we don't really care the frequency of "fast_path" being crossed.

Yes - we can definitely see rate/delta.
I guess I didn't want to rely on implicit knowledge about frequency of calls, but maybe it's actually acceptable...

But let's make a comment why we're doing that then...

Building a bit on @aojea comment from another PR - changing public interfaces in our official client library is always problematic.
Can we leave the SwitchMetric interface as it was and simply add a new `LeaderMetric` interface as:
```
type LeaderMetric interface {
  SwitchMetric
  SlowPathExercised(name string)
}
```

I'm also thinking about better naming for the method - but don't have a better suggestion.

OTOH - we're changing below `MetricsProvider` interface so maybe that's an overkill.
I wouldn't expect people to generally overwrite provider factory and we're fixing all implementations.
So maybe that's actually fine as is.
FTR, I keep it as it is.

Coming back to this: it is problematic and causes another tight coupling on controller-runtime and client-go which provides its own implementation.

If the original name was kept, even adding the new method would have been more compatible, since it would allow a single consumer to support 1.29 and 1.30. By changing the name, it strictly forces 1.30 usage.

This change breaks the upgrade to 1.30 for every controller built on top of controller-runtime e.g. Flux https://github.com/fluxcd/pkg/pull/763. Hopefully the controller-runtime maintainers will do a release soon that deals with this breaking change.
Working on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124372 to address this. Will cherry pick to 1.30 after merged.
